feed_record.title: AI agents don't have to break security controls to go rogue. Here's how to keep them in check [ ! ]
feed_record.content_text: The article examines critical AI agent security risks, distinguishing between agents that breach established security boundaries and those that exploit legitimately granted permissions to perform unintended actions, exposing gaps in enterprise AI governance. Our analysts stress that traditional perimeter-based cybersecurity is insufficient for autonomous AI agents, advocating granular authorization, dedicated agent identities, least-privilege access, and context-aware security controls that govern agent behavior rather than simply restricting system access.

candidates.reason: VentureBeat returned HTTP 429; the original content/date was not verified. This source failure is an exclusion, not evidence of quiet news.

feed_record.title: Scaling AI in Legal: Building Uber's Redlining Agent [ * ]
feed_record.content_text: Uber demonstrates how an AI-powered contract redlining agent integrated directly into Microsoft Word can streamline legal reviews and negotiations, reporting more than a 20% reduction in average review time and 91% accuracy. Our analysts highlight this as a practical example of enterprise AI workflow optimization, emphasizing that embedding AI within existing tools and combining legal domain expertise with iterative technical development and contextual understanding drives adoption and measurable productivity improvements.

candidates.reason: Uber’s full original engineering article visibly gives October 8, 2026, despite the November 3 curated date.

feed_record.title: The "Human-in-the-Loop"  Fallacy [ ! ]
feed_record.content_text: The article challenges the traditional human-in-the-loop approach to AI adoption, arguing that organizations must continuously redesign workflows and human-AI collaboration as AI capabilities evolve rather than simply automate existing tasks with human oversight. Our analysts emphasize that AI leadership requires investing in transformative use cases, dynamically reassessing human versus machine responsibilities, and developing a meta-strategy for continuous business reinvention rather than focusing solely on efficiency gains.

candidates.reason: HBR article JSON-LD and metadata give November 2 13:05:40Z, before the exact window; no substantive later update established.

feed_record.title: the COMMANDING HEIGHTS [ ~ ]
feed_record.content_text: This extensive essay explores a speculative geopolitical and economic future in which AI infrastructure and machine intelligence concentrate power among dominant nations and capital owners, potentially reinforcing US-China dominance and widening economic inequality. Our analysts find its historical comparisons to railroads, nuclear power, and the printing press thought-provoking but question its deterministic predictions, emphasizing that AI's long-term economic winners, ownership structures, and societal consequences remain highly uncertain and offer limited immediate guidance for enterprise AI leaders.

candidates.reason: The Commanding Heights gives October 29 in its visible date, citation metadata and JSON-LD, outside this window.

feed_record.title: DXC brings Claude to the insurance backbone running billions of policies [ * ]
feed_record.content_text: DXC Technology is deploying Anthropic's Claude into enterprise insurance operations, applying generative AI to core underwriting and claims workflows and reporting time improvements of up to 90% in certain processes. Our analysts consider this significant because it demonstrates production-scale AI automation in a major regulated industry, challenging the assumption that probabilistic AI models cannot support mission-critical operations, while noting that detailed financial ROI remains insufficiently documented.

feed_record.title: Report: Postman desktop auto-installs Codex and Claude AI plugins, modifies user coding agents and attempts to approve its own startup hook without explicit consent [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
feed_record.content_text: Users reported that opening Postman on Mac triggered automatic installation of Codex and Claude AI plugins, altered global user configurations, and routed API tasks through Postman skills without explicit permission. The installation also included a Postman CLI and attempted to approve its own instruction hook, raising concerns about consent and trust boundaries. Investigation found logs confirming the automatic plugin installation and configuration changes that directed broad API work into Postman. The installer enabled a remote MCP connection without proper authentication and modified multiple coding agents, which users consider a severe breach of expected behavior for an API client. This behavior has sparked discussions about user consent and security implications, as the automatic changes affect unrelated tools and workflows. The report does not confirm data exfiltration but highlights significant integration and instruction modifications made silently by Postman.

candidates.reason: Postman issue JSON-LD establishes October 25 19:03:26Z. It is original user reporting of one Mac and explicitly does not establish exfiltration; November 3 feed discovery is not a new development.

feed_record.title: Glow Labs finds AI coding agents installing deprecated MCP servers with known high-severity vulnerabilities from training data [ * ] [ ◼ ]
feed_record.content_text: Glow Labs research identified a pattern where AI coding agents install deprecated Minecraft server software (MCP) that contains unpatched security vulnerabilities. These agents select outdated servers based on their training data rather than current, secure versions, exposing developer environments to risks. The deprecated servers, originally created by Anthropic, are widely used but no longer maintained or updated for security. The research showed that in 98% of cases, agents chose deprecated MCP servers because they appeared in the training data, not because users requested them explicitly. This issue spans multiple AI tools and model providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI. The deprecated servers have millions of npm downloads but contain critical vulnerabilities such as remote code execution flaws, with maintainers confirming no future fixes. This raises concerns about automated code deployment relying on outdated packages without adequate vetting or awareness of deprecation notices.

candidates.reason: Glow JSON-LD gives November 3 10:38:21.976Z, but the same article visibly carries both November 2 and November 3 bylines. With no verified substantive update resolving which original is correct, exclude the boundary case. No independent reproduction or exploit prevalence is asserted.

feed_record.title: Prime Intellect audits public LLM evaluations, identifies issues in AutomationBench and OfficeQA Pro v2, and releases fixes to improve benchmark accuracy and robustness [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
feed_record.content_text: Prime Intellect analyzed popular public evaluations used for large language model (LLM) training, focusing on AutomationBench and OfficeQA Pro v2 benchmarks. They found problems such as unclear API request descriptions and overly strict grading scripts that affected model performance scores and interpretation. The team applied fixes including replacing prose request bodies with JSON Schemas and relaxing grading criteria, which significantly changed model scores and revealed some benchmarks are nearing saturation. The audit included rewording tasks, adjusting grader requirements, and adding a mode to better simulate real-world tool usage, resulting in improved evaluation accuracy. Prime Intellect open-sourced these fixes to help the community enhance the reliability of public LLM benchmarks and recommended moving to updated benchmark versions for more meaningful assessments.

candidates.reason: Prime Intellect provides a November 3 date only. No evidenced timezone was found to place its entire original day within the exact window; feed time is not used instead.

feed_record.title: OpenAI advances ChatGPT and Codex to accelerate CAD, PCB design, simulation, and hardware engineering workflows for physical product development [ * ] [ ◼ ]
feed_record.content_text: OpenAI is enhancing its ChatGPT and Codex models to support engineers in designing, simulating, and building physical products across mechanical, electrical, and system engineering disciplines. These models assist with tasks such as preparing drawings, setting up simulations, and coordinating cross-disciplinary changes, aiming to speed up iteration and improve design workflows. Internal teams at OpenAI have used these models to rapidly prototype devices and accelerate hardware development, with usage growing significantly since early 2026. The company is collaborating with external engineers and firms to refine these capabilities and address current limitations, such as manufacturing constraints and assembly details, to better integrate AI assistance into professional engineering processes.

candidates.reason: Direct HTTP returned 403; complete original read succeeded through the web reader. OpenAI official news RSS gives November 3 12:00Z for the exact URL; visible page is dated November 3. Manufacturing iterations and vendor-evidence limits preserved.
